text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: CI failures affecting multiple hotfix pipelines. Triggering oncall (kevin).

kevin (eng-oncall): getting the page. tons of GH Actions runs failing during artifact restore and package install. Errors: 502 from api.github.com and 403 from npm.pkg.github.com and ghcr.io.

maria (sre-oncall): joining bridge. can someone paste a snippet of a failing log? need to see if it's auth or upstream 5xx.

luke (devex): pasted: ```
Error: GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/@our-org/secret-lib - 403 Forbidden
Error: failed to pull image from ghcr.io/our-org/service: 502 Bad Gateway
```

jess (platform): this blocks our hotfix release for a live customer incident. We need a mitigation that doesn't rely on GitHub Package publishing or Actions runners. Ideas?

oliver (support): customers are on hold. ETA requests coming in. Please prioritize.

maria (sre-oncall): quick triage: check https://www.githubstatus.com and GH incident page. Also confirm if runner machines themselves are OK (heartbeat) or if actions control plane is degraded.

github-status-bot: GitHub Status: "Partial Service Disruption: GitHub Actions and GitHub Packages experiencing errors and auth failures." https://www.githubstatus.com/incidents/abcde

maria (sre-oncall): opening GitHub support case (GHS-654321). tagging severity-high. Meanwhile we'll attempt: 1) build/publish via internal artifact mirror (S3) and deploy from there; 2) if publishing image to GHCR fails, push prebuilt docker tar to s3 and load on nodes; 3) consider running CI on local self-hosted runner to avoid Actions control plane if runners are the issue.

kevin (eng-oncall): experimenting with local run of the pipeline on our k8s self-hosted runners. started `make ci-hotfix` on a runner pod. If that completes we can push the artifact out of band.

luke (devex): I'm building the hotfix locally and will push the artifact to s3. commands: ```
docker build -t service-hotfix:2026-03-15 .
docker save service-hotfix:2026-03-15 | gzip > svc-hotfix.tar.gz
aws s3 cp svc-hotfix.tar.gz s3://redwood-emergency/hotfixes/2026-03-15/
```

jess (platform): good. I can modify the deploy job to pull the tarball and load into containerd on the nodes via an init job. I'll open a rollback-safe branch `infra/emergency/hotfix-2026-03-15`.

oliver (support): telling affected accounts: "We're experiencing a third-party outage (GitHub Actions and Packages) which is delaying automated hotfix releases. We're applying a manual deployment process and expect resolution within ~1 hour. We'll update if timelines change."

kevin (eng-oncall): local runner finished building but publishing to GHCR fails with 403 on push. pushing tar to s3 succeeded.

maria (sre-oncall): ok proceed with s3 preload plan. Luke/Jess coordinate on a preloader job. I'll keep the GitHub case open and escalate if needed.

luke (devex): preloader job created in `infra/playbooks/emergency-preload.yml`. It downloads `s3://redwood-emergency/hotfixes/2026-03-15/svc-hotfix.tar.gz` and runs `ctr -n=k8s.io images import - < svc-hotfix.tar.gz` on each node. Not ideal but workable.

jess (platform): kicking off canary using the preload. Deploy run: manual by jess -> canary us-west-2 (2 pods). deploy-bot: `Deployment initiated (manual) by jess: hotfix-2026-03-15 -> canary-usw2 (2/2)`. logs link: https://deploy.redwood.local/67890

maria (sre-oncall): monitoring errors, traces, and customer-facing SLOs. If canary stable for 10-15m, expand.

oliver (support): updating customers: hotfix now in canary, ETA for full rollout 30-40m pending canary checks.

github-status-bot: Update: GitHub actions recovering for some customers; auth errors and package API still seeing intermittent 4xx/5xx.

kevin (eng-oncall): note: when we attempted to switch npm registry to our internal mirror via `npm config set registry https://internal-registry.local`, one scoped package still tried GH Packages due to lockfile `resolved` entries. had to patch lockfile to point at internal mirror. worth a followup automation.

luke (devex): confirming canary healthy after 14m. bumping to 20% and will keep watch.

maria (sre-oncall): handing monitoring to jess for the next 30m; I'll stay on the GitHub case and coordinate exec comms. Handoff note: watch for any CI runs that may auto-trigger image publish; those can fail and spam alerts.

jess (platform): canary at 20% (us-west + us-east subset). no regressions in customer metrics. logs good. moving to 50% in 10m unless alerts kick in.

oliver (support): communicating to customers that the workaround is in place and that we'll republish official GHCR images post-recovery. closing immediate support escalations.

kevin (eng-oncall): follow-up todos: 1) add fallback attempt in CI to use internal artifact mirror on GH Packages 4xx/5xx spike; 2) create a runbook and checklist for s3 preload + loader; 3) add monitoring alert for GH Packages 4xx/5xx rate. filing infra tickets.

maria (sre-oncall): creating runbook entry: "GitHub Actions/Packages outage - emergency deploy using S3 preload". scheduling tabletop with platform/devex to test end-to-end.

github-status-bot: Update: "Mitigations in place; partial recovery" - some customers reporting success; GH continuing to investigate auth failures.

jess (platform): expanding rollout to 100% for affected clusters. monitoring steady.

incidents-bot: Incident INC-2026-0315-02 created. Severity: High -> Mitigated (hotfix delivered via emergency artifact path). Postmortem scheduled.

maria (sre-oncall): closing the bridge for now. We'll keep the GitHub ticket open until full recovery. Thanks everyone for fast coordination. :clap: 

oliver (support): will include timeline and customer impact counts in the postmortem notes.

kevin (eng-oncall): handing over to next oncall in ~90m. leaving checklist and follow-ups in the incident doc.

jess (platform): final note: please don't delete the emergency artifact until we republish to GHCR; tag it with `hotfix-2026-03-15-ephemeral`.

maria (sre-oncall): agreed. post-incident: need automation to sanitize lockfiles to prefer internal mirrors when GH Packages error spikes detected.

incidents-bot: Post-incident tasks: create postmortem ticket and assign to maria/kevin/jess/luke/oliver."
